raw: | A mapping sourced from a **message definition** cannot be authored at all — MDL has `with json structure` and `with xml schema` and no third form — and `describe` of an existing one silently omits the source clause while still producing output that PARSES, so `describe` → `exec` rebuilds the mapping bound to nothing | 74 of the 327 mapping documents in the demo apps use one (the second-largest gap after the array root), 70 of them in the silent-loss class. The document is `MessageDefinitions$MessageDefinitionCollection` — a COLLECTION, which is why the reference is three parts (`Module.Collection.Definition`) — and it is derived from the **domain model**, not a payload sample: every node names an entity or an attribute and carries two names, its own (`Emails`) and the singular one its items take (`Email`) | `mdl/executor/mapping_messagedefinition.go` (`findMessageDefinition`, `messageDefPaths`, the two builders), `mdl/backend/modelsdk/messagedefinition_read.go`, `model/types.go` (`MessageDefinitionCollection`, and `XmlPath` on both mapping element types) | **A message-definition mapping stores BOTH path families** — that is the whole reason it needs its own builder rather than a branch of the JSON one: `json=(Array)\|(Object)\|From` beside `xml=Emails\|Email\|From`. The rules, measured on AgentCore.MesDef_Email / .MesDef_WorkflowDetails and Email_Connector.MD_EmailTemplate: an unbounded node contributes `ExposedName\|ExposedItemName` to the XML path and `ExposedName\|(Object)` to the JSON one, a single node contributes `ExposedName` to both, and the ROOT is the asymmetry — its own name is in the XML path but the JSON one is just `(Array)\|(Object)`. `model.ImportMappingElement`/`ExportMappingElement` had **no XmlPath field** and every writer hardcoded `""`, so that had to be added and carried on both engines' read and write paths first. **Do not "helpfully" drop the body**: the definition fixes entity, attributes and names, so a bodyless "map everything" form is tempting — measured, six of the ten real message-definition mappings map every exposed node and four map a strict subset (58 of 96, 27 of 30, 28 of 30, 26 of 27), so it would be lossy for 40% of them. `modelsdk/gen/messagedefinitions` already models the whole tree and decodes real documents unchanged (zero entries in `keyaudit_test.go`), so the read is one `mprread.ListUnitsWithContainer` call; the legacy engine has no parser and **refuses rather than returning an empty list**, because empty reads as "this project has no message definitions" and turns a real reference into a bogus "not found". The oracle is a Studio Pro mapping over the SAME definition: authoring `AgentCore.MesDef_Email.Email` from MDL reproduces `AgentCore.Email_Import` element for element. Repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/mapping-263-message-definition-source.mdl`, tests `mdl/executor/mapping_messagedefinition_test.go`. Issue ako/mxcli#263 |
